details: A recent European intelligence report indicates a potential "explosive" banking crisis in Russia, largely due to the strains of its war economy. In response, the European Union is reportedly preparing its 21st package of sanctions. These new measures are expected to target Russian banks and, notably, cryptocurrency networks, with the aim of preventing the evasion of existing sanctions through digital assets. The United Kingdom has also recently sanctioned crypto exchanges suspected of facilitating illicit financial activities related to Russia's conflict in Ukraine.
title: EU Prepares New Sanctions Targeting Russian Banks and Crypto Networks

details: The transition period for the European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) officially concluded on July 1, 2026. This landmark regulation now requires all crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) operating within the EU to be fully authorized. Consequently, any crypto firm that has not secured the necessary authorization must cease its activities or wind down operations in the region. This move aims to establish a unified regulatory framework, enhance market integrity, and provide greater investor protection across the European crypto landscape.
title: MiCA Regulation Enforcement Begins in EU, Unauthorised Crypto Firms Must Cease Operations

details: Seven member countries of OPEC+, including major producers Saudi Arabia and Russia, have announced an increase in oil production by 188,000 barrels per day. This expansion in supply coincides with the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping lane, which has allowed previously delayed oil shipments to move, significantly boosting the global inventory of oil in transit. These factors are collectively contributing to a downward pressure on international crude oil prices. Additionally, Iran has indicated plans to impose service fees for passage through the strait.
title: OPEC+ Boosts Oil Production as Strait of Hormuz Reopens, Pressuring Prices

details: The U.S. Department of the Treasury has taken action by imposing sanctions on the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC), a major Brazilian criminal organization. The sanctions target the network's involvement in laundering over $30 million in illicit drug proceeds, with funds being moved using cryptocurrency wallets between Florida and São Paulo. This action underscores the continuous efforts by global authorities to track and combat the use of digital assets in illegal financial activities and reinforce regulatory oversight in the crypto space.
title: US Treasury Sanctions Brazilian Criminal Network Using Crypto for Laundering
